newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures firmer as gas oil rallies.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures firmer as gas oil rallies.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were firmer on Thursday after U.S. markets opened, as strong gas oil prices dragged the energy complex higher, traders said.
December Brent stood at $22.30 a barrel at 1524 GMT, 15 cents up on the day, after reaching a high at $22.48. November gas oil was $4.25 up at $219.25 a tonne.
"It is gas oil," one IPE dealer said. "And it's being squeezed."
Dealers said the reported squeeze was conspiring with good demand for gas oil from Germany as well as the opening of arbitrage opportunities to Asian markets, to push prices higher.

The Brent/gas oil crack spread for December had ballooned out to $5.92 a barrel, compared with a low of $4.82 on Tuesday, and the backwardation between November and December had widened to $8.25 a tonne, compared with $6.25 at Wednesday's close.
U.S. markets opened higher but broadly in line with London traders' expectations, brokers said. "Those markets are reflecting products," one said.

Bullish technical factors were adding a further layer of support, brokers said. The only negative aspect to the market, from a technical point of view, was a fear that Brent may still be tempted to test support at around $22.00 a barrel.
